title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 8th edition — relative intensity table
claims: Heart rate reserve (HRR) is the difference between maximal heart rate and resting heart rate.
Moderate exercise intensity is defined as 40–59% of heart rate reserve, equivalent to 64–76% of maximal heart rate.
Hard (vigorous) exercise intensity is defined as 60–84% of heart rate reserve.
The target heart rate for a given relative intensity is calculated from heart rate reserve plus resting heart rate.
The table presents relative intensity as a percentage of heart rate reserve and as a percentage of maximal heart rate, alongside ratings of perceived exertion and metabolic equivalents.
